flags.observation: "I'm Uncle FrizzleBob" sets a male narrator; Style A specifies a female lead, so voice and persona clash in variant A.
"If you already know Flexner, Gehlen and Gladio" announces the dog whistles as a roster; all three are card words anyway, so no insider reward.
"Everybody else: dance, I'll keep it short." is generic filler that could appear in any song at all.
"D.U.M.B.s" as a dotted acronym leaves delivery ambiguous: spelled letters or one word.
"the contractors wear Rolexes" lands without its contrast half from the card, so the punch is weaker than printed.
Opener "Gehlen orders fear." states a link not on either card as fact inside the frame.
"keep people afraid, do the terrorizing" compresses the card's twist into a flat list; the reversal logic is lost.
"Hoover, plus sand." winks at the listener and adds an image not in the card art; strains the straight-face tip.
"Flexner standardized medicine" makes a person the agent where the card credits a report; minor shift.
"Genial." left as printed; sung in English it reads as friendly, flipping the intended German sense.
"mob looks like scouts selling cookies" lost its comparative subject; the punch reads as a non sequitur.
"The pig banker grins." describes the card's own art; no therefore/but link from the previous card.
Event line drops the card's timing claim, so "not a conspiracy, just excellent planning!" has no setup to invert.
"the folks on the corkboard own the company" can read as affirming the corkboard figures really rule, not parodying the frame.
